research_question: Can a polynomial-time analytic upper-bound selector choose a single exact-DP fallback at every encountered W residual, keeping the original quadratic root budget without enumerating/materializing every exact-DP pivot; and do the finite Phi3/Phi4 potential candidates survive this cheaper scheduler?

motivation.Galil_1977_guard: pure Davis-Putnam can require exponentially many distinct clauses for any elimination order on an infinite CNF family, so one-variable descent alone is not a polynomial proof

deterministic_selector.on_W_residual: compute UB_S for every remaining variable and choose lexicographically minimum (UB_S,var)
deterministic_selector.restart: run frozen W policy after the chosen exact-DP fallback

potential_candidates_diagnostic_only.analytic_sufficient_Phi4_certificate: UB_S * V^4 < S * (V+1)^4, because exact DP leaves at most V-1 variables

preregistered_domain.root_reachable_cases: exactly the 15 X residual occurrences plus the independently reconstructed Y minimized residual core

local_structural_stress.source: truth-blind one-clause mutations of the Y core and selected X residual cores

preregistered_domain.reason: AA's n=64..80 all-pivot/root scan exhausted the 60-minute resource cap; AB isolates selector complexity before any renewed scale expansion

counterexample_semantics.ANALYTIC_SELECTOR_BUDGET_GAP_FOUND: min_x UB_S(x)>B at a W residual. This refutes this analytic certificate/selector under the frozen B; it does NOT prove that every exact DP pivot exceeds B.
counterexample_semantics.PHI4_CANDIDATE_FALSIFIED_WITHOUT_SELECTO: selected within-B pivot exists and is sound, but immediate Phi4 fails on an exact chosen step. This refutes Phi4 as a universal potential candidate, not the quadratic budget policy.
counterexample_semantics.RESIDUAL_AFTER_AT_MOST_V0_ANALYTIC_FALLB: scheduler remains residual despite each fallback removing at least one variable within the preregistered fallback horizon
